decisions.reason: Total loss at indices 20, 22, 24, 26, 28 (no voice comes out); partial or intermittent loss at indices 21, 23, 25, 27, 29 (words or moments without sound). Both are inside “perda total ou parcial da voz”.

Umbrella wording of the source (“qualquer alteração da voz”) and the batch/base convention of keying specific voice terms together with Disfonia. Direct for the partial-loss stories; for the total-loss stories it depends on reading absence of voice as an alteration (B019-04).
Each utterance states a change of the speaker's own voice compared with before (higher, breathy and weak, deeper, muffled, lower, thinner and weaker) with the voice still present.
Disfonia fits, but the utterances use the wording of un-keyed entries (B019-01, B019-03).
The utterance reports a voluntary increase in loudness and a normal voice at home; no voice alteration is stated (B019-02).
“Rouca e áspera” (30) and “tom áspero” (38) are the source description of Rouquidão. Not keyed (B019-01).
“Minha voz fica falhando … não chega a desaparecer completamente”: the denial excludes only total loss; the batch's Afonia stories 23 and 27 use the same verb (B019-01).
Weak or low voice without any moment of absent sound; 37 and 39 deny absence of sound or whispering. Border with “perda parcial” recorded in B019-05.
The utterance says the voice trembles involuntarily; the entry describes involuntary fine oscillations, “frequentemente” in the hands (B019-03).
The description (“Alteração no timbre da voz (disfonia)”) is broad, but the label is Rouquidão and no hoarse or rough voice is described (B019-06).

findings.issue: Indices 30 and 38 key Disfonia only. Index 30 says the voice “sai bem mais rouca e áspera”; index 38 says it “fica falhando e com um tom áspero … mas não chega a desaparecer completamente”. “Voz aspera ou rouca” is the source description of Rouquidão, a separate entry of the same block, and the term also exists under APARELHO ENDOCRINOLÓGICO. The base Rouquidão stories accept Rouquidão (both contexts) and Disfonia together, and the inventory caution reads “Uma rouquidão claramente descrita também admite disfonia”; here the reverse direction is missing. At index 38 the voice that keeps cutting out also matches the wording the batch itself uses for Afonia as partial loss (indices 23 and 27).

findings.issue: Index 31: “Na aula, percebi que precisava aumentar muito o volume para a turma me ouvir; em casa, minha voz costuma sair normal.” The speaker raises the loudness on purpose in a classroom. The utterance does not say that the voice was weaker, different or unresponsive; a voice change is implied only by the contrast with home and has an ordinary explanation (room size, noise). If read as a weak voice, it approaches Afonia's “perda parcial”. The clue is the source word “volume”.

findings.resolution: Passed. The reviewer accepts the dual key because the source itself treats Disfonia as the umbrella of the block (Rouquidão “é um tipo de alteração da voz”), the inventory cautions against treating partial loss, hoarseness and dysphonia as mutually exclusive, and the batch and base apply the same convention to Rouquidão and Rinolalia stories (index 40 shown as example). findings.issue: The source defines Afonia as “perda total ou parcial da voz” and Disfonia as including changes of “volume”. A weak or quiet voice sits on the border. The batch keys the Afonia stories with both terms, but the Disfonia stories with a weak or low voice (33 “soproso e fraco”, 37 “mais baixa … só mudou o volume”, 39 “mais fina e fraca”) with Disfonia only. findings.resolution: Reviewer's rule, applied consistently: Afonia is supported when the utterance reports words or moments with no sound, or a voice that disappears; a voice that is present but weaker, lower or breathy is Disfonia only. On that rule 33, 37 and 39 pass (37 and 39 explicitly deny absence of sound or whispering) and 21 and 25 are correctly Afonia. Index 38 falls on the Afonia side of the rule and is held (B019-01). The border is a teaching decision.

findings.issue: APARELHO ENDOCRINOLÓGICO > Rouquidão is described as “Alteração no timbre da voz (disfonia), comum em bócio volumoso ou hipotireoidismo grave.” Read by its description alone, it would cover any change of voice quality, such as the higher voice of index 32, the breathy voice of 33, the deeper voice of 34, the muffled voice of 36 and the thinner voice of 39.

findings.resolution: Passed with Disfonia only. The entry's label is Rouquidão; the reviewer reads the description as explaining hoarseness, not as a second umbrella entry, and none of the five utterances describes a hoarse or rough voice. A teacher who reads the endocrine entry by its description would need to add it to these stories.

findings.issue: The ten Afonia stories share one rationale (“A fala descreve perda total ou parcial da emissão vocal; isso também documenta alteração da voz no sentido amplo da entrada Disfonia.”), reused verbatim as the Afonia evidence rationale, and one Disfonia evidence rationale (“A mesma fala documenta alteração da qualidade vocal, conforme a definição impressa, sem causa presumida.”). The ten Disfonia stories share “A fala explicita alteração do tom, volume ou qualidade vocal, sem exigir perda total da voz.” None says whether the loss is total or partial, or which of pitch, loudness or quality changed. “Alteração da qualidade vocal” is inaccurate for the five stories in which no voice is produced (20, 22, 24, 26, 28).
findings.resolution: No rationale names another symptom or term, so there is no copy-paste leftover from another group; the texts are generic rather than wrong, except for the “qualidade” wording on the total-loss stories. Passing stories are not held for this. Since the app shows the rationale to the student, a story-specific sentence would teach more. For the held stories the rationale gaps are part of B019-01 to B019-03.

findings.issue: Index 23: in a video call, “minha voz falhava” and “palavras saíam sem som” can be read as a connection dropout. Index 24: the loss is stated only for singing. Indices 20 and 26: single episodes with no duration. Index 21: “tentar completar o que queria dizer” could, alone, suggest word-finding. Index 32: “principalmente quando converso com alguém” is unnatural. Index 33: “soproso” is near-technical and “meu som” is odd. Index 36: most people find their recorded voice strange; “nas mensagens de áudio” weakens the complaint. Indices 30, 31, 34 and 37 use the source's own words (“rouca”/“áspera”, “volume”, “tom”, “volume”) as the clue.
findings.resolution: None of these opens another term for the passing stories (30 and 31 are held for other reasons). Suggested polish for a later edit: 23 change the setting to a face-to-face conversation; 24 add that speaking was also affected; 36 compare with face-to-face speech; 32 drop the clipped clause.

findings.issue: Entries considered for indices 20–29: Afasias (“Alteração ou perda da capacidade de compreender ou produzir a linguagem (falada ou escrita) devido a uma lesão cerebral.”), Disartria (“Dificuldade mecânica para articular e pronunciar as palavras corretamente…”), Disritmolalia (“Perturbação no ritmo e no compasso da fala (como a gagueira).”), Rinolalia (two contexts), Dispneia, Ansiedade and Acuidade auditiva. findings.resolution: Reviewer agrees with the key. Each utterance keeps the intention to speak and the articulation (moving the mouth or lips, writing, knowing the lyrics) and loses only the sound, which separates loss of voice from loss of language, from difficult articulation and from a rhythm disorder. No utterance reports nasal voice, breathlessness, fear or the speaker's own hearing difficulty.

items.reasoning: A voz “está mais fina e fraca do que era” e “o som mudou”, sem que a pessoa esteja sussurrando: mudança de altura (mais fina) e de volume (mais fraca) em relação ao habitual, com voz presente. Corresponde a “alteração da voz, como tom, volume ou qualidade”. “Não estou sussurrando” afasta a leitura de voz perdida. Voz fraca fica na fronteira com “perda parcial da voz” (B019-05); como a fala não relata momentos sem voz, mantenho só Disfonia.
